questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes “mass spectrometry”?

options.label: A
options.text: The fragmentation of a bond adjacent to a heteroatom or carbonyl group in a mass spectrometer, forming a resonance-stabilized cation.

options.label: B
options.text: The most intense peak in a mass spectrum, assigned an arbitrary relative abundance of 100% against which other peaks are scaled.

options.label: C
options.text: The high-wavenumber region of an IR spectrum (4000 to 1500 cm-1) showing characteristic stretching frequencies for specific functional groups.

options.label: D
options.text: An analytical technique measuring the mass-to-charge ratios (m/z) of ionized molecules and their fragments to determine molecular formulas and connectivity.

questions.correct_answer: An analytical technique measuring the mass-to-charge ratios (m/z) of ionized molecules and their fragments to determine molecular formulas and connectivity.
questions.explanation: A accurate description of mass spectrometry is: An analytical technique measuring the mass-to-charge ratios (m/z) of ionized molecules and their fragments to determine molecular formulas and connectivity.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which organic chemistry term best matches this description? The radical cation formed when a high-energy electron collides with a molecule and expels one electron without fragmentation.

options.label: A
options.text: infrared spectroscopy

options.label: B
options.text: diagnostic region

options.label: C
options.text: fingerprint region

options.label: D
options.text: molecular ion (M+)

questions.correct_answer: molecular ion (M+)
questions.explanation: The best match is molecular ion (M+): The radical cation formed when a high-energy electron collides with a molecule and expels one electron without fragmentation.
